Under the directives of Mohammed bin Rashid, Dubai Humanitarian facilitates a new air bridge to deliver urgent WHO medical and health supplies to the people of Gaza. The first flight departed two days ago carrying 11 metric tonnes of essential medicines, followed by three additional flights carrying medical supplies, medicines, tents and fortified biscuits. The four flights form part of a wider operation through which Dubai Humanitarian will facilitate the delivery of around 150 metric tonnes of WHO medical and health supplies to Gaza in the coming weeks.

As part of the ongoing effort to ensure appropriate sanitary living conditions for civilians across the Gaza Strip, COGAT reached out directly to Gazan residents through its Arabic-language social media page and asked them to report locations where waste removal was urgently needed, as we have done with water distribution. Following the many responses received from the civilian population, COGAT reviewed the requests and coordinated with local and international partners to operate waste removal services in many areas across the Gaza Strip. Specifically, after many civilian reports from the area, waste was removed from Al-Nadim Street, the Al-Zeitoun neighborhood, the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood, and from the A. Dahra area to the Jasser building in Khan Yunis. The waste removals at these locations were not a one-time operation. International organizations and local authorities will continue to operate there on an ongoing basis to clear the waste and deal with health hazards. Projects such as this waste-removal operation and last month’s water supply project prove how this direct channel of communication helps identify specific needs on the ground and enables a faster and more focused humanitarian response.
